questions.question: According to Redux's principles, how should a component change global state?
options: Assign the new value directly to store.getState()
Call a setter exported by the store for that field
Dispatch an action describing what happened, which a reducer handles
Update React Context, which Redux then copies
questions.explanation: State is read-only. The only way to change it is to dispatch an action; a pure reducer then computes the next state.

questions.question: Which piece of state is the weakest case for putting in Redux?
options: Whether a single dropdown inside one form is open
The logged-in user's profile shown in the header and settings page
Cart items used by the header badge, product page and checkout
Notification counts updated from several features
questions.explanation: State used by only one component belongs in local useState. Redux is for state shared across distant parts of the tree.

questions.question: What does the modern Redux team recommend for writing Redux logic today?
options: The core redux package's createStore with hand-written switch reducers
Redux Toolkit, using configureStore and createSlice
React Context with useReducer instead of Redux
connect() with mapStateToProps for every component
questions.explanation: Redux Toolkit is the official, recommended way to write Redux. createStore is marked deprecated in the core types and points to configureStore.

questions.question: In the one-way data flow, what happens right after the reducer returns new state?
options: The action is sent back to the component that dispatched it
The old state is mutated to match the new state
The reducer calls setState on every component
The store saves it and notifies subscribers, which re-read the state they need
questions.explanation: The store saves the new state and calls its subscribers. UI subscribed via React-Redux re-reads its slice of state and re-renders if it changed.
